source-integrity.provenance: Q2 SEC exhibit and issuer results are primary; current valuation is a separate independent market-data origin
source-integrity.freshness: Q2 results published 2026-08-04; market valuation through 2026-09-25
source-integrity.sourceIndependence: SEC/issuer duplicate operating claims are collapsed to one issuer origin; StockAnalysis is used independently for current valuation only

thesisQuality.basis: Recurring cloud security/exposure management addresses a durable enterprise need; 11% growth and platform expansion support fit, while suite consolidation limits moat certainty.

financialOperatingMomentum.basis: Q2 revenue grew 11% to $182.2M, GAAP gross margin reached 83%, adjusted EBITDA was $83.8M and full-year revenue guidance was raised to $732M-$738M.

marketValuationOpportunity.basis: At $172.43 on Sep.25, trailing P/E was 29.93, forward P/E 21.47 and P/S 8.49; valuation is demanding relative to roughly 10-11% revenue growth despite strong margins.

catalystScore.basis: Raised 2026 guidance, AI-native Risk Operations Center adoption, federal pipeline and QFlex engagement provide several identifiable catalysts, but timing and conversion are not fully quantified.

governancePower.basis: Two sequential guidance raises and sustained profitability support execution credibility; current evidence does not establish exceptional long-duration capital allocation.

alignment2036.basis: Cyber exposure management, cloud security and security for AI address durable digital-infrastructure needs likely to persist across multiple 2036 scenarios.

crossDivisionLeverage.basis: One cloud platform spans asset, vulnerability, cloud, application, endpoint and compliance workflows, but current evidence does not quantify cross-sell durability.

bottleneckControl.basis: Integrated visibility, risk prioritization and remediation create workflow stickiness, but broader security suites remain credible substitutes and Qualys does not control a unique system bottleneck.

scenarioRobustness.basis: Cloud-delivered security and compliance remain useful across varied enterprise technology scenarios; consolidation into larger security suites is the principal concentration risk.

substitutionResilience.basis: Integrated platform depth and remediation workflows create moderate replacement barriers, offset by credible endpoint, cloud-security and broader-suite alternatives.

supplyChainResilience.basis: Cloud software delivery has limited physical supply-chain exposure; service infrastructure and third-party cloud dependencies remain but are less constraining than hardware supply chains.

pricingPower.basis: 83% GAAP gross margin and 46% adjusted EBITDA margin alongside double-digit growth provide strong observed evidence of value capture, though retention/pricing detail is not separately disclosed here.

riskEvidence.basis: Moderate growth, suite consolidation and unproven retention/cross-sell durability can weaken differentiation despite strong profitability and raised guidance.

dataConfidenceEvidence.basis: Fresh SEC/issuer operating results plus independent Sep.25 valuation cover core economics; retention, billings quality and competitive win/loss remain undisclosed and reduce confidence.

scoreRecord.thesis: Qualys combines durable cyber-exposure demand with unusually strong software margins and improving 2026 execution, but moderate growth and suite consolidation cap the moat and valuation upside.
scoreRecord.keyRisk: Broader security platforms could compress retention, expansion or pricing before Qualys proves durable reacceleration.
scoreRecord.nextCatalyst: Q3 2026 results and evidence that federal, QFlex and AI-native Risk Operations Center pipeline converts into sustained growth above the current range.
